n: Jacob turns to the faithful, especially the wounded wives and children. If they look to God steadily and pray in faith, he will comfort them, defend them, and bring justice.
The pure in heart can lift up their heads and “feast upon his love” forever if they stay steady.
But woe to the impure. Unless they repent, the land is cursed for them, and the Lamanites—who are not guilty of these sins—will scourge them.
Soon, without repentance, Lamanites will take their lands and the Lord will lead the righteous away—which later happened under the first Mosiah.

f.w: lead away the righteous out from among you

n: Jacob shocks his audience: the Lamanites they despise are more righteous than they are, because Lamanites have kept the law of one wife and sexual purity.

f.w: cursing which hath come upon their skins

n: Because the Lamanites keep this commandment, God will be merciful and they will one day be a blessed people.
Lamanite families love one another. Their hostility comes from their fathers’ traditions. So how are the Nephites better in God’s eyes? Healthy family love counts heavily with God.
Jacob warns that at God’s judgment the Lamanites may look purer than the Nephites. He turns his listeners’ prejudice back on them: what matters to God is the heart, not appearance.

f.w: their skins will be whiter than yours
f.g: A rhetorical reversal: by God’s standard of purity, the Nephites would come off worse. The Church today teaches that skin color is never a sign of God’s favor or disfavor.

n: God commands them to stop insulting Lamanites for their skin or their sins. They should remember their own sins and that the Lamanites’ condition came from their ancestors’ choices.
Remember your children: your example has hurt them, and your sins could lead them to destruction—and you would answer for it.

f.w: their sins be heaped upon your heads

n: Wake up! Jacob urges them to rouse their souls from spiritual death, escape hell’s pains, and avoid the “second death”—final separation from God.

f.w: awake from the slumber of death

n: Jacob adds that he preached much more against sexual sin and every kind of wickedness, warning of their terrible consequences.
Not even a hundredth of the people’s history fits here; their wars, conflicts, and kings are on the larger plates.
These are called the plates of Jacob, though Nephi made them. Jacob ends this sermon.

f.w: made by the hand of Nephi
